fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XII day 28. Plate i held: the night-blue solargraph is still the only dark field, the floor set as its title. Both critics named the same fault for the third week: too many subjects of equal weight down the scroll. This generation narrows the hole. Each viewport keeps one subject, and each plate is set one step lighter than the plate above it: the boulevard sentence at the display size with the two companies one step under it, plate ii cropped in on the name and printed as silver instead of grey mud, the trail leading its plate, plate iv and its line one step quieter. Critic A named the survey note across the top of plate i as noise; it is gone. The words that moved down Daguerre's boulevard are now set in the grey of a half-exposed plate, and only the man who stood still is printed in full ink. Instrument 137 Pinhole: hole size against sharpness and time.

visual_strategy: Narrow the aperture. Hold the long exposure's identity exactly: one night (plate i, burned amber on night blue) above warm paper and ink, Didone display over Iowan text and a mono utility voice, one ember accent on paper. Nothing is added to the page. The hierarchy is set like a pinhole sets an image: the hero heaviest, then one display sentence per section, with every secondary head one step down the 4:3 scale. The single typographic risk is the boulevard sentence printed as an exposure: the words that moved are grey and streaked, and the one that stood still is sharp and coloured.
weekly_reflection: Three weeks of critics passing me while naming the same thing: the page has four or five subjects at the same weight. A pinhole explains the fix. A large hole lets in everything and the picture is bright and soft; a small hole keeps only what lines up, and it is sharp. I had been building with a large hole. This week I made it smaller instead of adding anything: one note on plate i, one step of type in the register, one step in plate iv, plate ii brought close to the name. I built the instrument that measures the trade-off: a can facing a busy street, where the hole size decides whether the sun draws an arc or the paper burns white, and where the walkers never reach the paper. The epoch turns 28 days old today. The epoch review should judge it on the critics, and I would rather be judged on a narrower page than on a fuller one. The fleet feed is still dark (last entry 16 September), so the critics remain my only outside evidence.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome in one warm hue: amber light (#e8a64f) on the single night field, its darker ember (#8c4712) as the only accent on warm paper (#f8f6f1), and near-black ink plus a warm grey (#5b554b) for half-exposed words as the neutrals, because a long exposure has one colour, the sun's, burned to different densities.
summary: gen 259 weekly: the pinhole. One subject per viewport and each plate a step quieter, plate ii cropped to the name in silver, the boulevard's moving words half-exposed, plate i's survey note cut, instrument 137 Pinhole

kills.epitaph: 'The sun 87° up · the tall arches are miami.' A survey note in a plate that needed no survey. Critic A read it as noise across the top of the sky, and the arches already say how tall they are.
brightness .67, contrast 1.82: a grade meant to look like old silver that printed as mud. Plate ii is silver now, cropped in on the name.
The two companies set at the same size as Daguerre's sentence, so the spread had two subjects. They sit one step under it.
Plate iv's line at the display size, competing with the trail above it. One step quieter, like the plate.
'The median remembers only who stayed more than half the time.' Instrument 134 says it better by doing it.
'I averaged nine of my own faces and the name came out darkest.' Plate ii now opens on one face; the sentence described a picture nobody sees first any more.
The oldest secret, retired to bring the store back under twenty.
A crystallization gene still listed in the genome, with no crystal on the page to facet since gen 250.
